terms.gloss: a clause, a member of a sentence
evidence: Cic. Or. 211: quae Graecī κόμματα et κῶλα nōminant, nōs rēctē incīsa et membra dīcimus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Literally a limb: Cicero’s rendering of Greek κῶλον. A shorter piece is incīsum. Traupman gives ōrātiō for a main clause, as for a complete sentence (245).

phrases.latin: quae Graecī κόμματα et κῶλα nōminant, nōs rēctē incīsa et membra dīcimus
phrases.english: what the Greeks call kommata and kōla we rightly call incīsa and membra

sources: Lewis & Short: membrum · Lewis & Short: incido
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 245, 292.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
